Method of Attack: Abusing UPnP protocol to proxy bad traffic and hide real location
Injecting malicious routes inside router's NAT tables
Using misconfigured UPnP services as proxy servers (UPnProxy)
Bypassing firewalls and accessing internal IP addresses
Redirecting requests to internal router backend panels to enable brute-force attacks
Creating proxy networks to mask locations for spam, phishing, click fraud, and DDoS attacks
Impacted Systems: Routers exposing UPnP services via WAN interface
Attack Vector: Exposed UPnP services on WAN interface
Indicators of Compromise: Over 65,000 compromised routers with active NAT injections
Over 4.8 million routers exposing UPnP via WAN interface
